transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-12-20 16:30 PST
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Tomas (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Priya (Aurora Procurement), Evan (Aurora Security), Sofia (Aurora Legal), Marcus (Aurora Cloud), Jamal (Aurora Product)

Summary (auto):
Quick readout between Redwood and Aurora on MSA/DPA expectations, pricing approval path, and preflight for a pilot POC. Security questions centered on KMS and data residency; legal asked about liability caps and audit logs. Next steps: Redwood to send DPA redline, SOC2 artifacts, and pricing workbook; schedule technical deep dive.

Topics:
- DPA redlines and liability limits
- SLA targets and uptime/latency SLOs for Dedicated vs Hosted
- Pricing approval path and committed capacity discounts
- KMS/HSM integration and key ownership models
- Pilot scope and acceptance criteria

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time right before the holidays. Um I'll do a 2-minute agenda, then pass to Tomas for the technical notes, and then we'll go into redlines and pricing.
[00:20] Priya: Sounds good. We have Sofia and Evan here for legal and security, and Marcus for architecture. Jamal maybe just listening for product constraints.
[00:30] Tomas: Hi. Quick note: we wanted to make sure we align on the two paths we discussed earlier — Hosted API for fast onboarding and Redwood Dedicated if you need reserved GPUs and data isolation. There is also Redwood Private which we can deploy into your VPC if you need air gap later.
[00:50] Marcus: When you say Redwood Private into our VPC, do you mean the control plane still runs in Redwood's cloud or everything is customer-managed?
[00:58] Tomas: Good q. The usual option is a private control plane where control plane is in your VPC and the runtime nodes can be customer-managed — depends on the package. For strict regulatory customers we can do fully customer-managed on-prem install, although that path adds ops overhead.
[01:15] Evan: We need to confirm KMS model. If keys are customer-managed, how are rotations and HSM backed keys handled? We also need to see the KMS integration docs and whether Redwood supports Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) to HSM.
[01:30] Maya: Absolutely. We'll share the KMS spec and the KMS integration whitepaper. Practically we support: Redwood-managed keys, customer-managed KMS via cross-account IAM, and an HSM-backed BYOK model in Private deployments.
[01:45] Sofia: On the DPA, typical asks: narrower liability cap for data breaches, specific audit rights, and a clause on deletion/return of data. Also we'll want retention windows pinned per data type.
[02:00] Maya: Understood. Our standard DPA includes retention controls and deletion APIs. Liability cap is usually tied to subscription fees; we can take a look at your standard MSAs and see where we can bridge.
[02:12] Priya: Timeline question — procurement needs signoff by mid-Jan to hit our Q1 integration plan. Is that realistic?
[02:20] Lena: From a CS perspective, we've onboarded customers within 3–4 weeks on Hosted. For Dedicated/Private there's a longer ramp (6–10 weeks) for provisioning and security reviews.
[02:33] Jamal: For the pilot we only need a small seat — basically 50k tokens/day equivalent and run a classification rerank flow against internal docs. We want to validate latency and accuracy.
[02:45] Tomas: For a rerank flow, latency is dominated by sequence length and model — we can pre-configure batching and caching to keep p95 under 400ms for small prompt sizes on Dedicated. On Hosted p95 is similar unless you hit burst limits.
[03:05] Marcus: Egress: we have strict egress controls; can Redwood guarantee data never leaves eu-west-1 for certain datasets?
[03:15] Maya: Yes, region pinning is supported. For Hosted we can pin to region-specific endpoints; for Dedicated/Private you get guaranteed residency because instances run in your region or your VPC.
[03:28] Evan: SOC2: can we get a copy of the report and any penetration test summaries?
[03:35] Maya: We'll send a SOC 2 type II report and the pen test summary under NDA. Also we have ISO27001 certificate in our security pack.
[03:45] Sofia: On the MSA redlines — we typically ask for: narrower indemnity, specific SLAs with credits, and data escrow for model weights if the vendor ceases operation. Do you have precedent on escrow?
[03:58] Maya: Data escrow for model weights is uncommon but we can discuss escrow for customer data snapshots. We do illustrate continuity plans in the contract appendix.
[04:10] Priya: Pricing: procurement needs a clear committed discount schedule, and a path for a pilot to convert into a committed reserved pool. Does Redwood do trial credits that convert?
[04:22] Maya: We issue trial credits for Hosted. For Dedicated we offer a short pilot (30 days) with provisional reserved pricing — if you convert to a committed monthly/annual reserved contract we can rebate pilot usage into committed credits. I'll send the exact workbook.
[04:36] Priya: Who signs the pricing? Is it commercial or legal?
[04:40] Maya: Commercial signs the SOW and pricing schedules, legal signs the MSA/DPA. Procurement typically needs both to be in sync.
[04:45] Marcus: Technical deep dive — we need to validate KV cache behavior for session-based apps. Tomas can you outline required telemetry for the benchmark?
[04:55] Tomas: Yep — we'll need sample prompt set, expected sequence lengths, p95 latency target, and a set of golden responses for quality checks (or an eval harness). We'll produce a benchmark plan and required S3 sample layout.
[05:10] Jamal: For golden responses are you saying we have to pick outputs? We prefer automated evals but okay.
[05:18] Tomas: Automated evals are fine; we recommend a small seed set of hand-curated prompts for regression tests.
[05:25] Sofia: On indemnity and liability caps — our standard is 3x fees or $5M whichever is lower, can Redwood accommodate?
[05:34] Maya: We typically propose a liability cap at 1x the fees for the prior 12 months. For enterprise we can discuss a higher cap on a case-by-case basis.
[05:44] Evan: Is there cyber insurance backing?
[05:46] Maya: Yes, we have a cyber policy; we'll share limits in the security pack.
[05:54] Priya: Procurement wants an approval path doc: who needs to sign, legal redline deadlines, and finance pricing approver list. Can Redwood prepare a short one pager?
[06:02] Lena: We can create a procurement intake checklist and a pricing approval matrix — we'll include it in the onboarding packet.
[06:12] Sofia: A few small transcription/notes: we also need explicit audit log retention windows and whether token-level logs are available.
[06:22] Tomas: Token-level traces are available in Dedicated and Private; in Hosted we provide aggregate metrics and can surface per-request traces subject to retention policies. We'll outline the retention and redaction knobs.
[06:35] Priya: On data deletion — can you show the API for purge and whether the purge covers logs and cached prefixes?
[06:44] Maya: Purge APIs can remove stored artifacts, and we have KV cache TTLs. We'll document exact behaviors.
[06:50] Jamal: A small thing — will we be charged for prefix cache storage if we use caching?
[06:55] Maya: Caching is accounted for in request-level metering; we'll clarify the unit economics in the workbook.
[07:00] Sofia: For timeline, if Redwood sends DPA redline by 12/23 and we return redlines by 12/30, can legal close in mid-Jan?
[07:08] Maya: That timeline seems feasible. Procurement's mid-Jan target lines up if the tech deep dive is scheduled for first week of January.
[07:18] Priya: One more question: competitors — we've seen OpenCloudAI run a similar dedicated offering. Why would we choose Redwood?
[07:25] Maya: Short answer: production-first runtime with predictable SLOs, transparent cost controls, and unified tooling across Hosted and Private. Also our Optimize toolkit provides batching/quantization recommendations to lower unit costs.
[07:40] Marcus: Can you quantify expected cost savings with quantization for our text-embedding workloads?
[07:45] Tomas: Rough ballpark: 30–50% lower GPU memory and ~20–40% lower per-token compute cost depending on model and quantization method. We'll model that in the workbook for your workload.
[07:58] Sofia: On retention of audit logs — we require 7 years for certain regulated data, is that supported?
[08:05] Maya: Seven years is long; we typically offer 1–3 years in standard packages and extended retention as an add-on. We'll include retention pricing.
[08:18] Priya: Great. Any final thoughts?
[08:22] Jamal: No, thanks.
[08:24] Maya: OK, recap of next steps: Maya to send DPA draft, SOC2 and security pack, pricing workbook. Tomas to prepare benchmark plan. Aurora to send MSA redlines and residency matrix. We'll aim to reconvene the week of 2026-01-05 for the technical deep dive.
[08:40] Sofia: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:45] Maya: Appreciate you, happy holidays!

Notes on transcription: There are a few minor transcription errors in names (Redwood Private mentioned sometimes as Redwood Privates), and some technical acronyms were expanded later in context.
